# prepspaces — Complete Technical Curriculum Manifest

> Website: https://prepspaces.com/
> Official Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/prepspaces/ (@prepspaces)
> Description: Comprehensive open educational curriculum covering 6 core systems engineering disciplines across 121 technical modules, architectural blueprints, interactive labs, and diagnostic frameworks.

---

# Track 1: System Design Masterclass

**Track Hub:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design
**Scope:** Comprehensive curriculum on large-scale distributed systems, high availability, database replication, microservices, consensus, traffic control, and architectural trade-offs.
**Total Modules:** 24

## Module 1: System Design Course & Architecture Interview Preparation
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design
- **Topic Summary:** Complete guide to designing scalable distributed systems, high availability, microservices, and system design interview questions.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 2: Requirements & Capacity Estimation Guide
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/requirements
- **Topic Summary:** Learn how to estimate throughput (QPS/RPS), storage volumes, bandwidth, and memory caches during system design interviews.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 3: Networking, APIs & Communication Protocols
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/networking
- **Topic Summary:** Deep dive into REST, gRPC, WebSockets, HTTP/2, HTTP/3, and TCP/UDP communication patterns in modern architectures.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 4: Monoliths vs Microservices Architecture
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/architecture
- **Topic Summary:** Compare monolithic architectures, modular monoliths, and microservices decomposition with real-world trade-off criteria.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 5: Relational Databases, NoSQL & Indexing Internals
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/databases
- **Topic Summary:** Master B-Trees, LSM-Trees, SQL indexing, NoSQL document/key-value stores, and database query optimization.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 6: Distributed Caching, Redis & CDN Strategies
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/caching
- **Topic Summary:** Master cache-aside, write-through, write-behind, LRU/LFU eviction, and distributed caching invalidation strategies.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 7: Database Replication, Partitioning & Sharding
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/replication
- **Topic Summary:** Master horizontal sharding, consistent hashing, single-leader vs multi-leader replication, and failover topologies.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 8: Object Storage, File Systems, Search Engines & Data Pipelines
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/storage
- **Topic Summary:** Master cloud object storage, distributed file systems, inverted index search engines, batch and streaming data pipelines, and modern lakehouse architecture.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 9: Distributed Systems, Clocks & Network Partitions
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/distributed-systems
- **Topic Summary:** Understand physical vs logical clocks (Lamport, Vector), network latency, timeouts, and CAP theorem nuances.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 10: Consistency Models, Linearizability & Quorum Systems
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/consistency
- **Topic Summary:** Deep dive into strict consistency, sequential consistency, causal consistency, eventual consistency, and quorum math (R+W > N).
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 11: Distributed Consensus & Raft Protocol
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/consensus
- **Topic Summary:** Interactive breakdown of distributed consensus, Paxos vs Raft, leader election, log replication, and split-brain defenses.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 12: Message Queues, Kafka & Event-Driven Architecture
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/messaging
- **Topic Summary:** Understand message brokers, RabbitMQ vs Apache Kafka, consumer groups, partitions, event sourcing, and delivery semantics.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 13: Distributed Transactions, 2PC & Saga Orchestration
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/transactions
- **Topic Summary:** Learn how to manage transactions across distributed microservices using Two-Phase Commit (2PC) and Saga patterns.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 14: Load Balancing, Rate Limiting & Traffic Management
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/traffic
- **Topic Summary:** Master L4/L7 load balancing algorithms, Token Bucket, Leaky Bucket rate limiting, circuit breakers, and backpressure.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 15: Scalability & Performance Modeling
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/scalability
- **Topic Summary:** Analyze system bottlenecks, vertical vs horizontal scaling, Amdahl's law, Universal Scalability Law, and performance tuning.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 16: Multi-Region Deployments & Disaster Recovery
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/multi-region
- **Topic Summary:** Design active-passive and active-active multi-region architectures, calculating RTO (Recovery Time Objective) and RPO.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 17: Reliability Engineering & Observability
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/reliability
- **Topic Summary:** Master metrics, distributed tracing, structured logging, SLA/SLO/SLI calculation, and high-availability design.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 18: System Design Security & Multi-Tenancy
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/security
- **Topic Summary:** Architect zero-trust networks, OAuth2/OIDC token verification, RBAC/ABAC authorization, and data isolation at scale.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 19: Real-Time Systems, WebSockets & Presence Servers
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/realtime
- **Topic Summary:** Design live presence platforms, collaborative editing architectures, and scalable WebSocket connection managers.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 20: Search Engines, Inverted Index & Vector Feeds
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/search
- **Topic Summary:** Understand inverted index engines (Elasticsearch), full-text retrieval, relevance ranking, and activity feed generation.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 21: AI Systems Design & Inference Serving at Scale
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/ai-systems
- **Topic Summary:** Architect production machine learning systems, model serving pipelines, GPU scheduling, vector databases, and RAG architectures.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 22: System Design Case Studies (URL Shortener, Chat, Feed)
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/case-studies
- **Topic Summary:** Full end-to-end architectural case studies: TinyURL shortener, real-time WhatsApp-style chat, and Twitter feed algorithms.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 23: Advanced System Design Case Studies (Uber, Netflix, Stripe)
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/advanced-case-studies
- **Topic Summary:** High-scale engineering deep dives: Ride-hailing dispatch, global video streaming CDN, and financial payment platforms.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 24: System Design Architecture Capstone Project
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/capstone
- **Topic Summary:** Synthesize all distributed system principles into a complete, enterprise-grade architecture specification and design doc.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

# Track 2: Cloud Computing Architecture

**Track Hub:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/cloud
**Scope:** Enterprise public cloud architecture across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud, covering VPC networking, serverless compute, storage, databases, and multi-cloud systems.
**Total Modules:** 13

## Module 1: Cloud Computing Course & Interview Preparation

## Module 2: Cloud Networking: VPCs, Subnets & Gateways

## Module 3: Cloud Compute: Virtual Machines to Serverless

- **Topic Summary:** Compare EC2 instances, spot instances, autoscaling groups, containers (ECS), and serverless execution models.

## Module 4: Cloud Storage: Object, Block & File Systems

- **Topic Summary:** Deep dive into AWS S3, EBS, EFS, storage lifecycle policies, encryption at rest, and cloud data tiering.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 5: Managed Cloud Databases: RDS, DynamoDB & Aurora
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/cloud/databases
- **Topic Summary:** Architect managed cloud database clusters with read replicas, multi-AZ failover, and global distributed tables.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 6: Well-Architected Cloud Framework
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/cloud/architecture

## Module 7: Deep AWS Engineering & Architecture Mastery
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/cloud/aws

## Module 8: Microsoft Azure Architecture & Enterprise Cloud
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/cloud/azure

## Module 9: Google Cloud Platform (GCP) Architecture
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/cloud/gcp

## Module 10: Multi-Cloud Strategy & Hybrid Architectures

## Module 11: Cloud Security, IAM & Zero-Trust Governance
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/cloud/security
- **Topic Summary:** Enforce least privilege IAM, secret rotation, key management (KMS), and automated cloud security posture management (CSPM).

## Module 12: Cloud Economics & FinOps Cost Optimization

# Track 4: Operating Systems Master Course

**Track Hub:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os
**Scope:** University-informed systems engineering based on MIT, Stanford, and CMU curricula. Kernel architecture, CPU scheduling, virtual memory, concurrency, file systems, and Linux internals.
**Total Modules:** 24

## Module 1: Operating Systems Master Course
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os
- **Topic Summary:** Master operating systems internals, kernel architectures, process scheduling, virtual memory, concurrency, and Linux systems programming.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 2: Module 2: Computer Architecture for OS Engineers
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/architecture
- **Topic Summary:** Master CPU execution, registers, privilege rings, interrupts, MMU page translation, TLBs, DMA, and system boot stages.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 3: Module 3: C Programming & Systems Programming Model
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/systems-programming
- **Topic Summary:** Master C memory models, virtual address space layouts, ELF binaries, static and dynamic linking, AddressSanitizer, and POSIX system interfaces.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 4: Module 4: OS Interfaces, System Calls & Program Execution
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/syscalls
- **Topic Summary:** Master system call transitions, file descriptors, fork, execvp, waitpid, process lifecycle, signals, pipes, and strace diagnostics.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 5: Module 5: Processes and Process Lifecycle
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/processes
- **Topic Summary:** Master process abstractions, kernel task_struct (PCB), 5-state transitions, context switching, orphans, zombies, and Linux /proc exploration.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 6: Module 6: CPU Scheduling and Performance
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/scheduling
- **Topic Summary:** Master FCFS, SJF, SRTF, Round Robin, Multilevel Feedback Queues (MLFQ), context-switch overhead, CPU affinity, and Linux EEVDF.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 7: Module 7: Threads and Multithreaded Programming
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/threads
- **Topic Summary:** Master POSIX threads (pthreads), shared vs private state, threading models (1:1, N:1, M:N), Amdahl's Law, and cache false sharing mitigation.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 8: Module 8: Concurrency, Synchronization and Deadlocks
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/concurrency
- **Topic Summary:** Master race conditions, critical sections, POSIX mutexes, condition variables, semaphores, C11 memory ordering, Coffman deadlock conditions, and linearizability.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 9: Module 9: Memory Hierarchy and Memory Allocation
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/memory
- **Topic Summary:** Master virtual address spaces, stack frames, heap allocators, first-fit vs best-fit vs buddy allocation, fragmentation, and cache locality.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 10: Module 10: Virtual Memory and Address Translation
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/virtual-memory
- **Topic Summary:** Master hardware MMU address translation, hierarchical page tables, PTE flags, TLB hit rates, Effective Access Time (EAT), and Copy-on-Write.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 11: Module 11: Demand Paging and Page Replacement
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/demand-paging
- **Topic Summary:** Master demand paging, minor and major faults, working sets, thrashing, FIFO, Optimal, LRU, Clock, Belady's Anomaly, and Linux memory pressure.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 12: Module 12: Advanced Memory, Virtual Machines and Containers
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/virtualization
- **Topic Summary:** Master memory-mapped I/O, huge pages, NUMA nodes, hypervisors, EPT/NPT two-stage translation, Linux namespaces, and cgroup v2 memory limits.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 13: Module 13: Filesystems and Storage Architecture
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/filesystems
- **Topic Summary:** Master files, directories, inodes, dentries, extents, journaling, crash consistency, VFS, page cache writeback, fsync, and ext4/XFS/Btrfs design.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 14: Module 14: Storage Architecture, I/O Scheduling & Performance
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/storage
- **Topic Summary:** Master HDDs, flash SSDs, NVMe parallel queues, Little's Law, Linux I/O schedulers, DMA, write amplification, and io_uring.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 15: Module 15: IPC, Pipes, Shared Memory & Signals
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/ipc
- **Topic Summary:** Master interprocess communication, anonymous pipes, named FIFOs, Unix domain sockets, POSIX shared memory, semaphores, signals, and backpressure.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 16: Module 16: Crash Consistency, Durability and Recovery
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/crash-consistency
- **Topic Summary:** Master crash consistency, page cache write ordering, fsync, atomic file replacement, journaling, copy-on-write, and disaster recovery validation.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 17: Module 17: Kernel Architecture & System Implementation
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/kernel-architecture
- **Topic Summary:** Master kernel internals, boot flow from UEFI to PID 1, system-call dispatch tables, trap handling, spinlock interrupt safety, and MIT xv6 vs Linux.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 18: Module 18: Linux Internals & Performance Diagnostics
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/diagnostics
- **Topic Summary:** Master Linux performance diagnostics, /proc, /sys, vmstat, iostat, perf, strace, PSI stalls, and evidence-based bottleneck triage.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 19: Module 19: OS Networking & Network I/O
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/networking
- **Topic Summary:** Master the Linux kernel network stack, TCP/UDP sockets, non-blocking I/O, epoll event loops, socket buffers, application backpressure, and network namespaces.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 20: Module 20: OS Security, Isolation & Reliability
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/security
- **Topic Summary:** Master Linux identities, capabilities, POSIX permissions, cgroup v2 limits, seccomp filters, Secure Boot, DoS defenses, and STRIDE threat modeling.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 21: Module 21: Advanced Synchronization & Multiprocessor Systems
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/advanced-sync
- **Topic Summary:** Master multiprocessor synchronization, spinlocks, atomics, lock-free queues, memory ordering, cache coherence, false sharing, NUMA, and RCU.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 22: Module 22: OS Design, Testing & Failure Analysis
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/testing
- **Topic Summary:** Master systems testing, component invariants, fault injection, ThreadSanitizer race detection, kernel panics, and performance regression gates.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 23: Module 23 Capstone: Build an OS Component (xv6/RISC-V)
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/capstone
- **Topic Summary:** Build, extend, and test an educational operating system component using MIT xv6 on RISC-V, system call traps, and engineering verification.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 24: Module 24: Final Capstone
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/final-capstone
- **Topic Summary:** Culminating operating systems engineering project. Implement bounded concurrent worker queues, performance diagnostic tools, or virtual memory simulators.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

# Track 5: Computer Networks & Internet Architecture

**Track Hub:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/networks
**Scope:** University-level networking based on MIT, Stanford, UC Berkeley, CMU, and Princeton. Physical transmission, Ethernet, IPv4/IPv6, BGP routing, TCP/UDP sockets, DNS, and network security.
**Total Modules:** 24

## Module 1: Module 1: Introduction to Computer Networks & Internet Architecture
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/networks
- **Topic Summary:** Master computer networks from physical signals and Ethernet switching to global BGP routing, packet switching math, TCP/IP protocols, and network security.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 2: Module 2: Network Models
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/networks/models
- **Topic Summary:** Master OSI 7-layer and TCP/IP 4-layer network models, protocol encapsulation, router frame re-framing, Wireshark packet dissection, and layered troubleshooting.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 3: Module 3: Physical Layer & Data Transmission
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/networks/physical
- **Topic Summary:** Master physical layer signals, Nyquist and Shannon channel capacity, optical power budgets, line coding (NRZ, Manchester, PAM-4), and ethtool transceiver diagnostics.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 4: Module 4: Data Link Layer & Ethernet Switching
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/networks/datalink
- **Topic Summary:** Master Ethernet frame structures, CAM table MAC learning, ARP resolution, 802.1Q VLAN trunking, Spanning Tree Protocol (STP), and Layer 2 link security.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 5: Module 5: IPv4 Addressing, Subnetting & Enterprise Planning
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/networks/ipv4

# Track: Blockchain Technology & Decentralized Systems (24 Modules)
> University-style curriculum based on Stanford CS251, MIT, UC Berkeley, Cornell, and NIST IR 8202.
> Track Overview: https://prepspaces.com/learning/blockchain

## Module 1: Introduction to Blockchain Technology
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/blockchain
- **Alternative URL:** https://prepspaces.com/courses/blockchain
- **Level:** Beginner to Intermediate | Theory + Practical | 6–8 hours
- **Topic Summary:** Centralized vs decentralized systems, distributed ledger technology (DLT), cryptographic hashing, SHA-256 properties, block anatomy, block linking, tamper-evident chains, and building a Python blockchain from scratch.
- **Key Concepts:** SHA-256 collision resistance, pre-image resistance, avalanche effect, Previous Hash linking, cryptographic verification, state machine replication.
- **Hands-On Lab:** Live interactive 4-block blockchain visualizer, real-time tampering simulator, and production-grade Python script with canonical JSON serialization and tamper detection.

---

## Module 2: Cryptography Fundamentals for Blockchain
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/blockchain/cryptography
- **Alternative URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/blockchain/crypto
- **Level:** Beginner to Intermediate | Mathematics + Programming | 10–12 hours
- **Topic Summary:** Mathematical foundations of cryptography, modular arithmetic, prime fields, finite groups, SHA-256 vs Keccak-256 vs SHA3-256, symmetric vs asymmetric encryption, secp256k1 elliptic curve scalar multiplication, ECDSA signing and verification, nonce reuse vulnerabilities, HD wallets (BIP-32), Ethereum and Bitcoin P2PKH address generation, binary Merkle trees, and logarithmic inclusion proofs.
- **Key Concepts:** One-way preimage and collision resistance, avalanche effect, ECDLP discrete log hardness, ECDSA (r, s) formulation, RFC 6979 deterministic nonces, X9.62 public key serialization, domain-separated Merkle proofs.
- **Hands-On Lab:** Live interactive Merkle tree builder with visual sibling proof explorer, live private key and address derivation simulator, and complete Python toolkit with zero third-party blockchain dependencies.

---

## Module 3: Distributed Systems & Consensus Mechanisms
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/blockchain/consensus
- **Alternative URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/blockchain/distributed-systems
- **Level:** Intermediate | Theory + Mathematics + Programming | 12–15 hours
- **Topic Summary:** Distributed computing fundamentals, node communication and failure models (crash, omission, timing, Byzantine), the Byzantine Generals Problem (n >= 3f + 1), Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) and quorum intersection (Q = 2f + 1), Proof of Work (PoW) mining difficulty and expected attempts, Nakamoto consensus and heaviest chain selection, Proof of Stake (PoS) validator committees, Gasper and slashing, Proof of Authority (PoA), Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT) pre-prepare/prepare/commit phases, temporary forks, chain reorganizations (reorgs), probabilistic vs explicit finality, Sybil attacks and defense, network partitions, Brewer's CAP theorem (CP vs AP), and the Fischer-Lynch-Paterson (FLP) impossibility result.
- **Key Concepts:** Safety vs liveness, quorum intersection (Q = 2f + 1), cumulative work fork choice, 16^d difficulty scaling, 2/3 stake supermajority, PBFT view changes, orphan blocks, mempool recycling, 51% attack threshold, selfish mining, asynchronous agreement impossibility.
- **Hands-On Lab:** Live interactive Byzantine Generals simulator with customizable traitors and quorum verification, real-time in-browser SHA-256 Proof of Work mining sandbox with tamper detector, Proof of Stake validator lottery and committee approval visualizer, CAP theorem network partition sandbox, and complete Python implementations of Proof of Work (`proof_of_work.py`) and Proof of Stake (`proof_of_stake.py`).

---

## Module 4: Bitcoin Architecture, Transactions & UTXO Model
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/blockchain/bitcoin-utxo
- **Level:** Intermediate | Theory + Systems Engineering | 10–12 hours
- **Topic Summary:** Bitcoin architecture, Unspent Transaction Output (UTXO) accounting model, transaction scripts (Script), mempool, block verification, Coinbase transactions, and halving cycles.
- **Key Concepts:** UTXO graph, Script stack execution (OP_DUP, OP_HASH160, OP_EQUALVERIFY, OP_CHECKSIG), P2PKH, P2SH, SegWit (BIP-141), transaction fees, block serialization.
- **Hands-On Lab:** UTXO pool visualizer, Bitcoin Script stack execution simulator, and transaction verification engine.

---

## Module 5: Ethereum & EVM Architecture
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/blockchain/ethereum-evm
- **Level:** Intermediate | Theory + Architecture | 10–12 hours
- **Topic Summary:** Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM), state transitions, account model, world state trie, Patricia Merkle trees, gas schedule, EIP-1559 fee market, and smart contracts.
- **Key Concepts:** Account state (nonce, balance, storageRoot, codeHash), modified Merkle Patricia Trie (MPT), gas limit vs gas price, base fee burning, priority tip, uncle blocks, and PoS consensus.
- **Hands-On Lab:** Live EVM state transition simulator, Patricia Trie lookup inspector, and EIP-1559 gas fee calculator.

---

## Module 6: EVM Deep Dive & Opcode Execution
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/blockchain/evm-internals
- **Level:** Advanced | Low-Level Systems | 12–15 hours
- **Topic Summary:** 256-bit EVM stack machine, volatile memory allocation, non-volatile storage slot layout, SSTORE/SLOAD gas mechanics, call opcodes (CALL, STATICCALL, DELEGATECALL), and bytecode disassembly.
- **Key Concepts:** Stack overflow/underflow, memory expansion quadratic cost, storage collision vectors, EVM word alignment, fallback and receive functions, revert reasons, and assembly Yul.
- **Hands-On Lab:** Interactive step-by-step EVM stack/memory/storage debugger and Yul bytecode tracer.

---

## Module 7: Solidity Programming Fundamentals
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/blockchain/solidity
- **Level:** Intermediate | Programming | 12–15 hours
- **Topic Summary:** Solidity 0.8+ syntax, value types, reference types (memory, storage, calldata), visibility specifiers, view and pure functions, function modifiers, events, custom errors, and contract inheritance.
- **Key Concepts:** ABI encoding/decoding, arithmetic checked math, reentrancy guards, event emission topics, interface definition, abstract contracts, and error handling with revert.
- **Hands-On Lab:** Browser-based Solidity compiler sandbox with unit assertion checking.

---

## Module 8: Advanced Solidity & Gas Optimization
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/blockchain/advanced-solidity
- **Level:** Advanced | Optimization & Security | 12–15 hours
- **Topic Summary:** Storage slot packing (256-bit word packing), calldata vs memory optimization, assembly Yul implementations, unchecked arithmetic blocks, memory caching of storage variables, ERC-7201 namespaced storage, and immutable patterns.
- **Key Concepts:** SLOAD/SSTORE gas reduction, tight variable packing, transient storage (EIP-1153), calldata slice manipulation, bitwise operations for permissions, and custom assembly routines.
- **Hands-On Lab:** Live gas benchmark comparator demonstrating 40%+ gas reduction across baseline vs optimized contracts.

---

## Module 9: Smart Contract Development & Architecture
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/blockchain/architecture
- **Level:** Advanced | Systems Design | 12–15 hours
- **Topic Summary:** End-to-end decentralized application architecture: factory pattern, registry pattern, pull payments over push payments, escrow state machines, OpenZeppelin integration, UUPS and Transparent upgradeable proxies, and The Graph event indexing.
- **Key Concepts:** Proxy delegatecall mechanisms, EIP-1967 storage slots, storage collision prevention, initialization vs constructor, emergency circuit breakers, and state machine transitions.
- **Hands-On Lab:** Interactive proxy upgrade simulator with storage slot validation.

---

## Module 10: Smart Contract Testing & Security
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/blockchain/testing
- **Level:** Advanced | Quality Assurance | 10–12 hours

- **Key Concepts:** Invariant testing, fuzz test input generation, vm.prank and vm.deal cheatcodes, stateful vs stateless fuzzing, coverage analysis, and CI/CD testing pipelines.
- **Hands-On Lab:** Live fuzz test runner diagnosing invariant violations.

## Module 11: Wallets, Keys & Transaction Signing
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/blockchain/wallets-keys
- **Level:** Intermediate | Cryptography & Security | 10–12 hours
- **Topic Summary:** Hierarchical Deterministic (HD) wallets (BIP-32), mnemonic seed phrases (BIP-39), standard derivation paths (BIP-44), ECDSA transaction signing, EIP-1559 envelopes, EIP-712 typed structured data signing, Sign-In with Ethereum (SIWE), and nonce management.
- **Key Concepts:** Entropy to mnemonic generation, master node derivation, public vs private child keys, replay attack mitigation (EIP-155), and typed structured hashes.
- **Hands-On Lab:** Live BIP-39 mnemonic generator, BIP-44 address explorer, and EIP-712 signing simulator.

# Track: Machine Learning Master Course (24 Modules)
> Comprehensive university-level and production-grade Machine Learning curriculum covering environments, NumPy linear algebra, Pandas data manipulation, EDA, regression, regularization, classification, decision trees, tree ensembles (Random Forests, XGBoost, LightGBM), SVMs, KNN, Naive Bayes, cross-validation metrics, feature engineering, Scikit-learn pipelines, clustering, dimensionality reduction (PCA, t-SNE), anomaly detection, recommender systems, time series forecasting, probabilistic ML, statistical learning theory, Optuna hyperparameter optimization, SHAP interpretability, and full end-to-end capstone engineering.
- Track Hub: https://prepspaces.com/learning/machine-learning
- Canonical Course URL: https://prepspaces.com/courses/machine-learning

## Module 1: Machine Learning Environment & Production Workflows
- URL: https://prepspaces.com/learning/machine-learning
- Concepts: Python virtual environments (venv, conda), Jupyter notebooks, Google Colab, project directory structures, GPU setup (CUDA, PyTorch/TensorFlow backend checks), Scikit-learn design patterns (Estimators, Transformers, Predictors, Pipelines), and reproducible random seed management.
- Implementation: Standardized ML project scaffold, requirements.txt, configuration management, and initial dataset loading verification.

## Module 2: NumPy & Numerical Computing for Machine Learning
- URL: https://prepspaces.com/learning/machine-learning/numpy
- Concepts: NumPy ndarray memory architecture, C vs Fortran order, strides, vectorization, SIMD instructions, broadcasting mechanics, tensor slicing, np.linalg matrix multiplication, eigenvalues, eigenvectors, SVD, and implementing loss functions (MSE, Log-Loss, Hinge) from scratch in pure NumPy.
- Implementation: Benchmarking vectorization vs Python loops, matrix transformations, and gradient computations.

## Module 3: Pandas & Data Preprocessing
- URL: https://prepspaces.com/learning/machine-learning/pandas
- Concepts: Series and DataFrame structures, memory optimization (downcasting dtypes, category types), loading CSV/JSON/Parquet, handling missing data (mean, median, mode, KNNImputer, iterative imputer), categorical feature encoding (One-Hot, Ordinal, Target), and feature normalization (StandardScaler, MinMaxScaler, RobustScaler).
- Implementation: Production-grade data cleansing and preprocessing pipeline handling messy raw data with edge-case protection.

## Module 4: Exploratory Data Analysis & Statistical Visualization
- URL: https://prepspaces.com/learning/machine-learning/eda
- Concepts: Descriptive statistics, parametric vs non-parametric distribution tests (Shapiro-Wilk, Kolmogorov-Smirnov), skewness, kurtosis, correlation metrics (Pearson, Spearman rank, Kendall tau), covariance matrices, pairplots, correlation heatmaps, box plots, IQR/Z-score outlier detection, and automated EDA reporting.
- Implementation: Systematic EDA notebook answering real-world business hypotheses with distribution plots and hypothesis testing.

## Module 5: Linear Regression & Gradient Descent
- URL: https://prepspaces.com/learning/machine-learning/linear-regression
- Concepts: Univariate and multivariate linear regression, Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) closed-form solution (Normal Equation), convexity of MSE cost function, Batch Gradient Descent, Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD), Mini-batch Gradient Descent, learning rates, momentum, R-squared, Adjusted R-squared, and residual analysis (homoscedasticity, normality).
- Implementation: Linear regression engine written from scratch with NumPy and verified against Scikit-learn LinearRegression.

## Module 6: Regularization, Ridge, Lasso & ElasticNet
- URL: https://prepspaces.com/learning/machine-learning/regularization
- Concepts: Bias-variance tradeoff, multicollinearity, ill-conditioned matrices, L2 Tikhonov regularization (Ridge Regression), L1 Lasso regularization (sparsity, feature selection, subgradient descent), geometric intuition of L1 vs L2 constraint regions, ElasticNet convex combination, and cross-validated alpha tuning (RidgeCV, LassoCV).
- Implementation: Comparing coefficient shrinkage paths across Ridge, Lasso, and ElasticNet on high-dimensional collinear datasets.

## Module 7: Logistic Regression & Classification
- URL: https://prepspaces.com/learning/machine-learning/logistic-regression
- Concepts: Binary and multiclass classification, Sigmoid/Logistic activation function, odds and log-odds (logit), Binary Cross-Entropy loss (Log-Loss), maximum likelihood estimation (MLE), decision threshold tuning, Softmax regression (multinomial), Precision, Recall, F1-Score, ROC curves, AUC-ROC, and PR-AUC.
- Implementation: Binary credit default classifier with calibrated probability outputs and custom decision threshold optimization.

## Module 8: Decision Trees & Tree Mechanics
- URL: https://prepspaces.com/learning/machine-learning/decision-trees
- Concepts: Non-linear decision surfaces, recursive binary splitting, Information Gain, Shannon Entropy, Gini Impurity, Variance Reduction for regression trees, ID3, C4.5, and CART algorithms, tree depth, minimum leaf samples, cost-complexity pruning (ccp_alpha), and decision path extraction.
- Implementation: Visualizing decision tree boundaries, interpreting feature importance, and pruning trees to prevent overfitting.

## Module 9: Ensemble Learning, Bagging, Random Forests & Boosting
- URL: https://prepspaces.com/learning/machine-learning/ensembles
- Concepts: Ensemble theory, Condorcet's jury theorem, variance reduction through bagging, Bootstrap Aggregating, Out-of-Bag (OOB) error estimation, Random Forests, feature subsampling, AdaBoost adaptive sample weighting, Gradient Boosted Decision Trees (GBDT), shrinkage learning rate, and tree boosting with XGBoost and LightGBM.
- Implementation: End-to-end benchmarking of Single Tree vs Random Forest vs Gradient Boosting vs XGBoost on fraud detection.

## Module 10: Support Vector Machines (SVM) & Kernel Methods
- URL: https://prepspaces.com/learning/machine-learning/svm
- Concepts: Maximum margin hyperplanes, functional and geometric margins, support vectors, hard vs soft margin SVM, slack variables, C regularization parameter, Lagrange multipliers, dual problem formulation, KKT conditions, and the Kernel Trick (Linear, Polynomial, Radial Basis Function RBF, Sigmoid).
- Implementation: Linear and non-linear classification with SVMs, gamma and C grid sweeps, and decision boundary visualization.

## Module 11: K-Nearest Neighbors & Naive Bayes
- URL: https://prepspaces.com/learning/machine-learning/knn-naive-bayes
- Concepts: Instance-based non-parametric learning, distance metrics (Euclidean, Manhattan, Minkowski, Cosine), curse of dimensionality, spatial partitioning data structures (KD-Trees, Ball Trees), Bayes' Theorem, conditional independence assumptions, Gaussian Naive Bayes, Multinomial Naive Bayes, and Laplace additive smoothing.
- Implementation: High-performance spam classification with MultinomialNB and KNN spatial indexing.

## Module 12: Model Evaluation, Validation & Metrics
- URL: https://prepspaces.com/learning/machine-learning/model-evaluation
- Concepts: Train/validation/test partitions, data leakage vectors, K-Fold cross-validation, Stratified K-Fold, GroupKFold, TimeSeriesSplit, confusion matrix decomposition, Type I vs Type II errors, Macro/Micro/Weighted F1, Cohen's Kappa, Matthew's Correlation Coefficient (MCC), and learning curve diagnosis.
- Implementation: Custom evaluation harness generating comprehensive classification and regression diagnostic reports.

## Module 13: Feature Engineering & Selection
- URL: https://prepspaces.com/learning/machine-learning/feature-engineering
- Concepts: Feature construction, non-linear interactions, polynomial features, log/Box-Cox/Yeo-Johnson power transforms, cyclical feature encoding (sine/cosine for time/day), target encoding with smoothing, filter methods (ANOVA F-test, Chi-square, Mutual Information), wrapper methods (Recursive Feature Elimination RFE), and embedded methods.
- Implementation: Automated feature engineering pipeline boosting baseline model performance across tabular benchmarks.

## Module 14: Scikit-learn Pipelines, ColumnTransformer & Custom Transformers
- URL: https://prepspaces.com/learning/machine-learning/pipelines
- Concepts: Software engineering best practices for ML, BaseEstimator and TransformerMixin interfaces, fit vs transform vs fit_transform, ColumnTransformer for parallel heterogeneous preprocessing, FeatureUnion, pipeline composition, preventing data leakage during CV, and model serialization (joblib, ONNX).
- Implementation: Production-ready Scikit-learn pipeline ingesting raw mixed-type data and outputting calibrated predictions.

## Module 15: Unsupervised Learning & Clustering
- URL: https://prepspaces.com/learning/machine-learning/clustering
- Concepts: Unsupervised learning taxonomy, K-Means clustering algorithm, Lloyd's optimization, K-Means++ centroid initialization, Elbow method, Silhouette Coefficient, Davies-Bouldin index, Hierarchical Agglomerative Clustering (dendrograms, Ward linkage), and DBSCAN density clustering (epsilon, min_samples, core/border/noise points).
- Implementation: Customer segmentation clustering with interactive 2D/3D visualizations and cluster profile summaries.

## Module 16: Dimensionality Reduction & PCA
- URL: https://prepspaces.com/learning/machine-learning/dimensionality-reduction
- Concepts: Curse of dimensionality, geometric projection, covariance matrix formulation, eigenvalue decomposition, Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), explained variance ratio scree plots, Kernel PCA, and non-linear manifold learning (t-SNE, UMAP).
- Implementation: Reducing 100+ feature space to principal components for downstream model speedup and visualization.

## Module 17: Anomaly Detection & Imbalanced Learning
- URL: https://prepspaces.com/learning/machine-learning/anomaly-imbalance
- Concepts: Anomaly detection paradigms, Isolation Forest (isolation depth, anomaly score), Local Outlier Factor (LOF density ratio), One-Class SVM, class imbalance challenges, Random Undersampling, Tomek Links, SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique), ADASYN, and cost-sensitive learning.
- Implementation: High-imbalance transaction fraud detection pipeline using SMOTE and Isolation Forests with PR-AUC optimization.

## Module 18: Recommender Systems
- URL: https://prepspaces.com/learning/machine-learning/recommenders
- Concepts: Utility matrices, sparsity challenges, memory-based collaborative filtering (User-User, Item-Item), Cosine vs Pearson similarity, model-based collaborative filtering, Truncated SVD, matrix factorization, content-based recommendation (TF-IDF, item embeddings), hybrid recommenders, and cold-start mitigations.
- Implementation: Building an e-commerce movie and product recommendation engine with top-N ranking metrics (Precision@K, MAP, NDCG).

## Module 19: Time Series Analysis & Forecasting
- URL: https://prepspaces.com/learning/machine-learning/time-series
- Concepts: Temporal data sequencing, trends, seasonality, cyclical patterns, additive vs multiplicative decomposition, stationarity testing (Augmented Dickey-Fuller ADF, KPSS), Autocorrelation Function (ACF), Partial Autocorrelation (PACF), AR(p), MA(q), ARMA, ARIMA(p,d,q), SARIMA, and walk-forward rolling window validation.
- Implementation: Energy demand and sales forecasting pipeline comparing classical SARIMA with gradient boosted time-series regression.

## Module 20: Probabilistic Machine Learning
- URL: https://prepspaces.com/learning/machine-learning/probabilistic-ml
- Concepts: Probability distributions (Gaussian, Bernoulli, Multinomial), joint, conditional, and marginal distributions, Bayes' Theorem, Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE), Maximum A Posteriori (MAP), conjugate priors, Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM), and the Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm.
- Implementation: Fitting Gaussian Mixture Models with EM for soft clustering and density estimation from first principles.

## Module 21: Statistical Learning Theory
- URL: https://prepspaces.com/learning/machine-learning/statistical-learning
- Concepts: Mathematical foundations of machine learning, Empirical Risk Minimization (ERM), true risk vs empirical risk, Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) learning, sample complexity, Vapnik-Chervonenkis (VC) dimension, Rademacher complexity, generalization error bounds, structural risk minimization, and No Free Lunch theorems.
- Implementation: Empirical simulation verifying VC dimension bounds and sample complexity curves across model families.

## Module 22: Hyperparameter Optimization & Explainable AI
- URL: https://prepspaces.com/learning/machine-learning/hpo-xai
- Concepts: Hyperparameter tuning algorithms: Grid Search, Randomized Search, Bayesian Optimization with Tree-structured Parzen Estimators (TPE) via Optuna, probability calibration (Platt scaling, Isotonic regression), Explainable AI (XAI), Permutation Feature Importance, Partial Dependence Plots (PDP), Individual Conditional Expectation (ICE), and SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations based on cooperative game theory).
- Implementation: Automated Optuna optimization study coupled with complete global and local SHAP model explanation dashboards.

## Module 23: Real-World Machine Learning Engineering & Case Studies
- URL: https://prepspaces.com/learning/machine-learning/case-studies
- Concepts: Machine learning system design, business objective translation, baseline model benchmarking, data validation, experiment tracking, pipeline orchestration, concept drift and data drift detection (Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, Population Stability Index PSI), low-latency REST and gRPC model inference serving, and Docker containerization.
- Implementation: Architecting, validating, and containerizing a real-world enterprise ML service with monitoring telemetry.

## Module 24: Final Machine Learning Capstone & Interview Mastery
- URL: https://prepspaces.com/learning/machine-learning/capstone
- Concepts: Full end-to-end Machine Learning capstone project: Customer Churn Prediction & Retention Optimization system. Translating telecom churn business problem into ML objectives, exploratory data analysis, robust ColumnTransformer preprocessing, multi-model benchmarking (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM), decision threshold optimization, SHAP interpretability for individual customer retention interventions, FastAPI production scoring service, and technical machine learning interview mastery defense.
- Implementation: Production-ready capstone repository with data pipelines, trained models, inference API, automated tests, and 10-slide architectural defense presentation.

- **Interactive Workbenches:** Buffer Pool & Cache Simulator, Index Internals Visualizer (B+ Tree vs LSM vs Hash), Query Execution & Join Engine Workbench, MVCC & Isolation Level Tester, WAL & Checkpoint Crash Recovery Lab, Performance Tuning Sizing Tuner & 15-Question Assessment.

- **Key Concepts:** Fact table grain, surrogate key generation, partial vs transitive dependencies, superkeys in BCNF, Star vs Snowflake trade-offs, SCD Type 2 dimension versioning, event time vs processing time, and schema registry compatibility.
- **Hands-On Lab:** Interactive ERD & schema inspector, normalization anomaly fixer (1NF-3NF), star vs snowflake join comparator, SCD Type 2 dimension simulator, event-driven streaming emitter, and comprehensive assessment.


### Module 7: Data Warehousing and Analytical Systems
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/data-engineering/data-warehousing
- **Topics Covered:**
  - 1. Introduction to Data Warehousing (Inmon 4 characteristics: subject-oriented, integrated, time-variant, non-volatile)
  - 2. Evolution of Data Warehouses (EDW -> Big Data Hadoop -> Cloud DW -> Lakehouse)
  - 3. Operational vs Analytical Databases (OLTP vs OLAP architecture and workload patterns)
  - 4. Data Warehouse Multi-Tier Architecture (7 functional tiers from sources to consumption)
  - 5. Enterprise Data Warehouse (EDW) governance, integration, and master data management
  - 6. Centralized and Distributed Analytical Warehouses
  - 7. OLAP Architecture & Multidimensional Analysis (Roll-up, Drill-down, Slice, Dice, Pivot, ROLAP vs MOLAP vs HOLAP)
  - 8. Multidimensional Data Modeling (Additive, semi-additive, non-additive facts & dimension attributes)
  - 9. Fact and Dimension Table Design (Transaction, periodic snapshot, accumulating snapshot, factless fact tables)
  - 10. Star and Snowflake Schemas (Denormalization vs normalized dimension hierarchies)
  - 11. Enterprise Data Marts (Dependent, independent, and hybrid data marts)
  - 12. Enterprise BI and Semantic Layer Architectures (Power BI, Tableau, Looker, Metabase, RBAC)
  - 13. Columnar Storage Mechanics (Projection pushdown, dictionary/RLE encoding, vectorized SIMD execution)
  - 14. Massively Parallel Processing (MPP) Architecture (Leader/coordinator, compute workers, hash/even/all data distribution, network shuffle, skew mitigation)
  - 15. Data Warehouse Partitioning Strategies (Range, list, hash, date-trunc partitioning, and partition pruning)
  - 16. Clustering and Sorting (Micro-partition pruning, Snowflake cluster keys, BigQuery clustered tables, Redshift sort keys, ClickHouse MergeTree order keys)
  - 17. Materialized Views (Precomputed query persistence, incremental refresh, aggregate and join views)
  - 18. Query Optimization for Analytical Workloads (Execution plans, projection pushdown, predicate pushdown, join optimization)
  - 19. Warehouse Performance and Cost Optimization (Compute auto-suspend, sizing, workload management, storage compression)
  - 20. Snowflake Architecture (Storage-compute decoupling, virtual warehouses, micro-partitions, Time Travel, zero-copy cloning)
  - 21. Google BigQuery Architecture (Serverless slot model, Capacitor columnar format, Colossus storage, BigLake)
  - 22. Amazon Redshift Architecture (Leader node, compute nodes, RA3 managed storage, slices, KEY/EVEN/ALL distribution styles)
  - 23. ClickHouse Architecture (MergeTree storage engine, parts, primary sparse index marks, background merges, distributed tables)

  - 10. Delta Lake Architecture (_delta_log transaction log, JSON commit actions, checkpoints, ACID transactions, optimistic concurrency)
  - 11. Apache Hudi Architecture (Timeline instants, file groups, base Parquet files, log files, Copy-on-Write vs Merge-on-Read, compaction)

  - 13. ACID Transactions in Data Lakes (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability over object storage)
  - 14. Snapshot Isolation & MVCC (Multi-Version Concurrency Control, non-blocking readers, consistent analytical views)

  - 16. Schema Evolution (Adding, dropping, renaming columns, type widening, field IDs, schema enforcement vs evolution)
  - 17. Partition Evolution and Partitioning Strategy (Partition pruning, avoiding over-partitioning, versioned partition specs)
  - 18. Metadata Catalogs (AWS Glue Data Catalog, Hive Metastore, Unity Catalog, crawlers, table discovery)
  - 19. Small File Problems and Compaction (Streaming file explosion, metadata overhead, OPTIMIZE file rewriting)

### Module 11: Distributed Data Processing with Apache Spark
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/data-engineering/spark-processing
- **Topics Covered:**
  - 1. Introduction: What is distributed data processing? (Single-machine limits vs. multi-worker cluster parallelism, node partitions, fault tolerance, data locality)
  - 2. Big Data Processing Fundamentals (5 Vs: Volume, Velocity, Variety, Veracity, Value; Batch, Streaming, Micro-batch; Horizontal vs. Vertical scaling)
  - 3. Hadoop Ecosystem Overview (HDFS, YARN, MapReduce, Hadoop Common, Hive, HBase, Pig, Sqoop, Flume, ZooKeeper, Spark vs. Hadoop comparison)
  - 4. MapReduce Programming Model (Map key-value pairs, Shuffle and Sort, Reduce aggregations, Combiners, MapReduce execution flow and limitations)
  - 5. Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) (NameNode metadata, DataNode blocks, 128 MB block size, block replication factor 3, read/write pipelines, High Availability)
  - 6. Apache Spark Architecture (Unified analytics engine, Driver program, Cluster Manager, Worker nodes, Executors, Tasks, Job/Stage/Task hierarchy)
  - 7. Spark Driver and Executors (Driver orchestration, query planning, stage scheduling, executor computation, client mode vs. cluster mode)
  - 8. Spark Clusters (Standalone, YARN, Kubernetes deployments, CPU core allocation, local[*] vs. distributed execution)
  - 9. RDD Architecture — Resilient Distributed Datasets (Immutability, partitions, parallelize(), map/filter/union transformations, lineage graph fault recovery)
  - 10. DataFrame and Dataset APIs (Distributed named columns, Catalyst optimization, createDataFrame, select/filter/withColumn/groupBy, strongly typed Datasets in Scala)
  - 11. Spark SQL (Temporary SQL views, Catalyst Optimizer, logical/physical plans, predicate pushdown, column pruning, explain(True))
  - 12. Transformations and Actions (Lazy transformations vs. eager actions show/count/collect/write; Narrow vs. Wide transformations)
  - 13. Lazy Evaluation (Execution DAG planning, optimization passes, debugging strategies, schema validation)
  - 14. Data Partitioning (Partition count tuning, CPU utilization, repartition() full shuffle vs. coalesce() partition reduction, storage partitionBy)
  - 15. Shuffling and Data Exchange (Redistribution across partitions, network communication, disk I/O serialization, shuffle minimization best practices)
  - 16. Joins and Aggregations in Spark (Inner, Left, Right, Full Outer, Left Semi, Left Anti joins; sum/avg/count aggregations; multi-column joins)
  - 17. Broadcast Joins (Large fact table + small dimension lookup, broadcast() function, avoiding shuffles, broadcast threshold limits)
  - 18. Caching and Persistence (cache() vs. persist(), MEMORY_ONLY, MEMORY_AND_DISK, StorageLevel, unpersist(), cache optimization guidelines)
  - 19. Data Skew and Optimization (Straggler tasks, skewed keys, salting with rand() suffixes, broadcast joins, Adaptive Query Execution (AQE))
  - 20. Spark Memory Management (Unified Memory Management, Execution Memory vs. Storage Memory, JVM heap, OOM errors, spilling to disk, GC overhead)
  - 21. Spark Performance Tuning (Early filtering, column pruning, Parquet, broadcast joins, partition count tuning, Kryo serialization, Spark Web UI diagnostics)
  - 22. Processing Parquet and Lakehouse Data (Row-based vs. column-based storage, Parquet row groups/chunks/pages, Delta Lake, Iceberg, Hudi, Medallion Architecture Bronze/Silver/Gold)
  - 23. Building Large-Scale Distributed Pipelines (End-to-end ingestion, raw storage, distributed cleaning, data validation, Gold publication, monitoring)
  - 24. Practical Project — Large-Scale E-Commerce Sales Analytics Platform (PySpark session, Bronze landing, schema validation, window row_number() deduplication, broadcast join, Silver write, Gold sales metrics)
  - 25. Practical Labs and Assignments (Labs 1-5: RDDs, DataFrames, Joins, Optimization, Lakehouse pipelines)
  - 26. Advanced Assignments (Large-scale log analysis, fraud detection, Customer 360, real-time payment analytics, skew optimization)
  - 27. Interview Preparation — Apache Spark (Fundamental, programming, optimization, and lakehouse interview questions)
  - 28. Recommended Learning Resources (Official Spark docs, Hadoop docs, Parquet spec, Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg, PySpark API)
  - 29. Final Module Summary (Synthesis of cluster computing, memory management, and production distributed pipelines)

  - 16. Monitoring Workflow Execution (Airflow UI views, task states, duration monitoring, alerting integrations, Prometheus and Grafana metrics)

  - 19. Production Airflow Deployment (Dev vs Prod, Docker containerization, Kubernetes Helm deployment, production checklist)

  - 1. Introduction to Stream Processing (Continuous processing over unbounded events, operations: filter, transform, enrich, aggregate, join, pattern detection, message consumption vs stream processing)

  - 15. Checkpointing and Recovery (Periodic state snapshots, recovery workflows, Flink checkpoint barriers aligned/unaligned, checkpoints vs savepoints, Spark checkpointLocation)
  - 16. Exactly-Once Processing Concepts (At-most-once, at-least-once, exactly-once boundaries, Flink two-phase commit sinks, Spark foreachBatch batchId deduplication, idempotent PostgreSQL upserts)
  - 17. Apache Flink Architecture (JobManager: ResourceManager, Dispatcher, JobMaster; TaskManagers, Task Slots resource scheduling, operator chaining, parallelism, RocksDB state backend, deployment modes)

  - 21. Real-Time Analytics Dashboards (Window aggregation for visualization efficiency, metrics: revenue, transactions, operational lag; frontend updates: polling, SSE, WebSockets)

## Module 15: Distributed Systems for Data Engineers
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/data-engineering/distributed-systems
- **Topics Covered:**
  - 1. Introduction to Distributed Systems (Single-machine limitations vs distributed cluster, workload division, partial failure, concurrency, scalability, 10-item overhead trade-offs)
  - 2. Distributed Computing Architecture (Client-server, multi-tier presentation/application/data layers, master-worker coordinator model, peer-to-peer, microservices boundaries, vertical vs horizontal scaling)
  - 3. Distributed Processes and Communication (IPC mechanisms, synchronous request-response vs asynchronous messaging, network failure modes, latency vs throughput, performance metrics)
  - 4. Client-Server Architecture and Remote Procedure Calls (RPC internal mechanics, client/server stubs, serialization, gRPC over HTTP/2, Protocol Buffers, JSON-RPC, XML-RPC, RPC vs REST, failure modes)
  - 5. Network Communication and Serialization (Serialization workflows, JSON, XML, Apache Avro schemas, Protobuf IDL, Apache Parquet columnar storage, TCP connection-oriented reliability vs UDP datagrams, serialization payload size math)
  - 6. Distributed Storage Systems (HDFS NameNode and DataNode block architecture, block sizing, S3 object storage buckets and keys, distributed databases Cassandra/Spanner/CockroachDB, storage vs computing separation)
  - 7. Data Partitioning (Partition pruning, horizontal vs vertical partitioning, range partitioning, hash partitioning (Hash(Key) % N), list partitioning, round-robin, sharding vs partitioning, data skew and hot partition mitigation)
  - 8. Data Replication (Replication factor N, synchronous replication acknowledgements vs asynchronous replication lag, failover risks, replication in Kafka/Cassandra/Postgres, replication vs point-in-time backups)
  - 9. Leader and Follower Architecture (Primary-replica write coordination, leader reads vs follower reads, failover mechanisms, split-brain problem and fencing, multi-leader regional replication conflicts)
  - 10. Consistency Models (Strong consistency, linearizability vs serializability, eventual consistency convergence, read-your-writes, monotonic reads, monotonic writes, consistency levels comparison)
  - 11. Strong Consistency and Eventual Consistency in Practice (E-commerce race conditions, inventory reservation vs product view counts, business operation consistency mapping)
  - 12. CAP Theorem (Consistency linearizability, Availability, Partition Tolerance trade-offs, CP vs AP behaviors during network split, PACELC theorem, common CAP misconceptions)
  - 13. Quorum-Based Systems (Read/write quorum formula R+W>N, strict overlap proof, majority voting Q=floor(N/2)+1, fault tolerance thresholds, Cassandra tunable consistency)
  - 14. Fault Tolerance (Hardware, software, network, data, and human failures, redundancy, checkpointing in distributed compute engines, fault tolerance vs high availability)
  - 15. Failure Detection (Heartbeats, adaptive timeouts, false positive detections, liveness, readiness, and dependency health checks, failure detection vs recovery)
  - 16. Consensus Fundamentals (Agreement, validity, termination, safety vs liveness, Raft consensus algorithm: leader election, candidate states, replicated log replication, Paxos comparison)
  - 17. Distributed Coordination (Distributed locks, lease expiration, fencing tokens for stale worker protection, coordination services ZooKeeper, etcd, Consul)
  - 18. Retry Mechanisms and Idempotency (Fixed-delay, exponential backoff formula Delay=Base*2^attempt, jitter randomness against thundering herds, mathematical idempotency f(f(x))=f(x), idempotency keys, SQL ON CONFLICT upserts, idempotency vs exactly-once)
  - 19. Backpressure (Producer-consumer throughput imbalance, queue accumulation, flow control, rate limiting, buffering, Kafka consumer lag metrics, Spark Streaming micro-batch rate limits, backpressure vs buffering)
  - 20. Message Delivery Guarantees (At-most-once, at-least-once with retry duplication, exactly-once transactional scope, Kafka idempotent producer, transactional commits, consumer offset management commit strategies)
  - 21. Distributed System Reliability (Reliability vs availability, uptime formula, the 5 nines 99.999% downtime tables, single points of failure, load balancing, bulkheads fault isolation, circuit breaker states CLOSED/OPEN/HALF-OPEN, disaster recovery RPO and RTO, SLIs, SLOs, and SLAs)
  - 22. Putting Everything Together: Real-World Distributed Data Engineering Architecture (Complete real-time e-commerce architecture mapping all 21 distributed systems principles across Kafka, Python workers, distributed storage, and analytics)
  - 23. Practical Laboratory (Lab 1: Python Multiprocessing Worker Pool, Lab 2: Dockerized Apache Kafka Messaging, Lab 3: Leader-Follower Replication Simulation, Lab 4: Enterprise Event Processing Platform Mini-Project)
  - 24. Common Mistakes in Distributed Systems (15 Production fallacies: assuming distributed is faster, ignoring idempotency, treating retries as harmless, CAP misinterpretations, omitting fencing tokens, etc.)
  - 25. Important Interview Questions and Answers (30 Comprehensive technical interview Q&As with full system design explanations)
  - 26. Recommended Learning Resources (Official documentation for Kafka, Spark, Hadoop, gRPC, Cassandra, Raft, PostgreSQL, etcd, Kubernetes)
  - 27. Final Revision — Module 15 (Complete 21-topic revision summary table)

  - 1. Advanced Backtracking: Decision Trees, Pruning with Fast Boolean Lookups, N-Queens O(1) Diagonal Tracking, Sudoku Constraint Propagation
  - 2. Branch and Bound: State-Space Exploration, Best-First Search with PriorityQueue, Upper/Lower Bounding, 0/1 Knapsack & Traveling Salesperson
  - 3. Divide and Conquer: Problem Splitting, Subproblem Recombination, MergeSort Inversion Counting, Closest Pair of Points O(N log N)
  - 4. Binary Search on Answer: Monotonic Feasibility Functions f(k), Range Search [low, high], Ship Packages within D Days, Painter's Partition, Split Array Largest Sum
  - 5. Monotonic Stack Patterns: Next Greater / Smaller Element in O(N), Monotonic Increasing vs Decreasing, Largest Rectangle in Histogram, Trapping Rain Water
  - 6. Monotonic Queue Patterns: Sliding Window Extrema in O(N) using ArrayDeque, Double-Ended Eviction, Sliding Window Maximum, Constrained DP Optimization
  - 7. Graph Problem-Solving Patterns: Comprehensive Decision Matrix (Unweighted BFS, 0-1 BFS, Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford, DAG Topo Relax, DSU, Bipartite Coloring)
  - 8. Dynamic Programming Problem Classification: 1D Linear, 2D Grid, String/Subsequence, Knapsack/Subset, Interval DP, Bitmask DP, Digit DP, Tree DP
  - 9. Tree DP Patterns: Subtree Recurrences, Post-Order DFS, Maximum Independent Set (take vs skip), Tree Diameter, Centroid Decomposition
  - 10. Greedy Proof Techniques: Greedy Stays Ahead Method, Exchange Arguments, Matroid Theory Foundations, Safe Choice Invariants
  - 11. Mathematical Problem-Solving: Modular Arithmetic & Inverse, Euler's Totient Function φ(n), Matrix Exponentiation for Linear Recurrences O(K³ log N), Inclusion-Exclusion Principle
  - 12. Advanced Array Techniques: Difference Array Range Updates [l, r] += x in O(1) with Prefix Sum Recovery, 2D Prefix Sums, Coordinate Compression
  - 13. Offline Query Processing: Query Reordering, Two Pointers with Offline Sorting, Mo's Algorithm Sqrt-Decomposition (Block Size √N, O((N + Q)√N) Time)
  - 14. Competitive Programming Fundamentals: Fast I/O (BufferedReader, StringTokenizer), Time Limit Invariants (~10⁸ ops/sec), Memory Management, Edge Cases
  - 15. Problem Constraints Analysis: Deriving Algorithmic Complexity from N (N ≤ 20: O(2ⁿ), N ≤ 100: O(N³), N ≤ 10⁵: O(N log N), N ≤ 10⁹: O(log N) or O(1))
  - 16. Selecting the Right Data Structure: Systematic Trade-Off Matrix (ArrayList, LinkedList, ArrayDeque, PriorityQueue, TreeSet/TreeMap, Trie, DisjointSet, SegmentTree)
  - 17. Selecting the Right Algorithm: Core Algorithmic Paradigms vs Problem Signatures Decision Hierarchy
  - 18. Multi-Pattern Integration: Chaining Binary Search + BFS/Dijkstra, Two Pointers + Sliding Window, Monotonic Stack + Dynamic Programming
  - 19. Common Pitfalls & Antipatterns: Integer Overflow in Mid Computations, Off-by-One in Binary Bounds, Unpruned Recursion, Mutating Shared State
  - 20. 35 Practice Problems Across 4 Levels: Pattern Recognition, Advanced DS & Algorithms, Advanced Optimization & DP, Contest Multi-Pattern
  - 21. 15 Assessment MCQs with Scenario Explanations and Instant Diagnostic Scoring
  - 22. 8 Interactive Workbenches: N-Queens Backtracker, Binary Search on Answer Lab, Monotonic Stack Studio, Monotonic Queue Maximum Simulator, Graph Pattern Classifier, Tree DP Independent Set Visualizer, Difference Array Range Updater, Mo's Algorithm Sqrt-Decomposition Simulator

### Module 22: Java Collections, JVM & Performance Engineering
URL: https://prepspaces.com/learning/java/collections-jvm
Topics Covered:
  - 1. Java Collections Framework Deep Dive: Iterable and Collection Hierarchies, Separation of Map Hierarchy, Utility Algorithms, and Fail-Fast Iterators
  - 2. ArrayList Internals: Dynamic Resizing Mechanics, 50% Capacity Growth Formula, Element Shifting on Insertion/Deletion, and Amortized O(1) Appends
  - 3. LinkedList Internals: Doubly Linked Node Structure, O(1) First/Last Operations vs O(N) Traversal, and Hardware Cache Locality Disadvantages
  - 4. HashMap Internals: Bit Spreading Hash Function (hash ^ (hash >>> 16)), Power-of-Two Table Capacity, Separate Chaining, Treeification at 8 Entries, 0.75 Load Factor, and equals()/hashCode() Contracts
  - 5. TreeMap and TreeSet: Red-Black Tree Invariants, Logarithmic Operations O(log N), NavigableMap Range Queries (firstKey, lastKey, floorKey, ceilingKey, lowerKey, higherKey)
  - 6. PriorityQueue Implementation: Complete Binary Min-Heap Array Storage, Sift-Up on offer() in O(log N), Sift-Down on poll() in O(log N), and Max-Heap Reverse Comparators
  - 7. Concurrent Collections: Thread-Safety in JCF, ConcurrentHashMap Lock-Free CAS & Bucket Synchronization, CopyOnWriteArrayList for Read-Heavy Registries, and BlockingQueue for Producer-Consumer Systems
  - 8. Java Memory Model (JMM): Visibility Problems, Volatile Variable Happens-Before Semantics, Non-Atomic Compound Increments, AtomicInteger CAS Loops, Monitor Locks (synchronized), and Object Immutability
  - 9. Stack and Heap Memory: Per-Thread JVM Stacks, Method Frames (Local Variables, Operand Stack), StackOverflowError, Shared Heap Memory, References vs Objects, and Metaspace
  - 10. Garbage Collection: Reachability Analysis from GC Roots, Weak Generational Hypothesis (Eden, S0/S1 Survivors, Tenured Old Gen), Mark-Sweep-Compact, Modern Collectors (G1, ZGC, Shenandoah), Stop-The-World Pauses, and Memory Leaks
  - 11. JVM Architecture: Bytecode Lifecycle (javac -> .class -> JVM), ClassLoader Subsystem, Runtime Data Areas, Execution Engine (Interpreter + JIT), and Native Interface (JNI)
  - 12. Class Loading Lifecycle: Loading, Linking (Verification, Preparation, Resolution), Class Initialization, Bootstrap/Platform/Application Loaders, and Parent Delegation Model
  - 13. JIT Compilation: Just-In-Time Native Compilation, Hot Methods, Tiered Compilation (Interpreter Tier 0 -> C1 Tiers 1-3 -> C2 Server Tier 4), Method Inlining, Escape Analysis (Scalar Replacement), and JVM Warm-up
  - 14. Java Performance Profiling: Latency vs Throughput Metrics, Java Flight Recorder (JFR), Java Mission Control (JMC), VisualVM, jcmd Diagnostics, and JMH Microbenchmarking Harness
  - 15. Object Allocation: Object Header Layout and Alignment Padding, Thread Local Allocation Buffers (TLABs), String Concatenation vs StringBuilder, Primitive Boxing Costs, and Pooling Antipatterns
  - 16. Time and Memory Optimization: Data Structure Selection, Eliminating Nested O(N^2) Loops, Collection Views vs Clones, BufferedReader Fast I/O, and Space-Time Tradeoffs
  - 17. Big-O vs Practical Performance: Why Asymptotics Fail in Hardware, Cache Locality, Object Dereferencing Costs, CPU Branch Prediction, and Allocation Churn
  - 18. Writing Efficient Java Code: Interface Type Declarations, Idiomatic Map Methods (getOrDefault, merge), Memory-Efficient Duplicate Filtering, and Baseline Measurement Workflows
  - 19. Worked Examples: K Largest Elements via PriorityQueue Min-Heap, Student Lookup Directory via HashMap, First Non-Repeating Character via LinkedHashMap
  - 20. 35 Practice Problems Across 4 Levels: Collections & Selection, Concurrency & JMM, JVM Memory & GC Diagnostics, JIT & Enterprise Performance
  - 21. 15 Assessment MCQs with Scenario Explanations and Instant Diagnostic Scoring
  - 22. 8 Interactive Workbenches: ArrayList Dynamic Resizer, HashMap Bucket & Collision Simulator, PriorityQueue Min-Heap Simulator, Collections Selection Matrix, JMM Visibility & Race Simulator, Generational GC Visualizer, JIT Tiered Compilation Engine, and Production Outage Diagnostic Studio

### Module 23: Technical Interview & Placement Mastery
URL: https://prepspaces.com/learning/java/interview-mastery
Topics Covered:
  - 1. Data Structures Interview Preparation: Interviewer Expectations, Core Data Structures (Arrays, Strings, Linked Lists, Stacks, Queues, HashMaps, Trees, Graphs, Heaps, Tries, DSU, Segment Trees), Time and Space Complexity Comparison Table, and Frequency of Testing
  - 2. Algorithms Interview Preparation: Algorithmic Categories (Searching, Sorting, Recursion, Backtracking, Greedy, Dynamic Programming, Graphs), Matching Problem Constraints to Asymptotics, and Choosing Between Linear Search and Binary Search
  - 3. Coding Interview Methodology: The Seven-Step Framework (Understand, Clarify, Brute-Force, Optimize, Complexity, Code, Dry-Run), Avoiding Premature Coding, and Collaborating with Interviewers
  - 4. Clarifying Problem Requirements: Input Format & Ranges, Negative Values, Floating Point Values, Duplicate Elements, Empty and Single-Element Inputs, Mutability of Inputs, Ordering Requirements, and Extreme Constraint Clarifications
  - 5. Brute Force to Optimized Solution: Establishing Correct Baselines, Identifying Redundant Computations, Transforming O(N^2) Nested Loops to O(N) via HashMaps (Two Sum), Trade-offs Between Memory and Execution Speed
  - 6. Complexity Explanation: Formulating Big-O Time and Space Bounds, Dominant Terms, Drop Constants, Recursion Stack Overhead, and Amortized Time Complexity (ArrayList dynamic resizing)
  - 7. Edge Case Analysis: Edge Case Discovery Methodology, Empty Inputs, Single Elements, Two Elements, All Duplicates, All Negative Numbers, Extreme Values (Integer.MAX_VALUE overflow), Large Inputs, and Comprehensive Checklist
  - 8. Dry Runs: Walking Through Logic Manually, Systematic Variable Trace Tables, Testing Normal and Boundary Inputs, Catching Off-by-One Pointer Errors Before Running Code
  - 9. Code Quality and Readability: Semantic Variable Naming, Avoiding Over-Engineering, Modular Helper Methods, Interface Types, and Idiomatic Java Standards
  - 10. Interview Communication: Think-Aloud Protocol, Structuring Explanations (Problem -> Naive -> Bottleneck -> Optimized -> Space/Time), Responding to Hints, Navigating Feedback, and Maintaining Composure
  - 11. Java Coding Interview Questions: Core Java Specifics, String Immutability and StringBuilder Efficiency, equals() and hashCode() Contract in HashMaps, OOP vs Interfaces, Abstract Classes, and Custom Comparators
  - 12. Arrays and Strings Interview Patterns: Two-Pointer Techniques (Palindromes, In-place Reversal), Sliding Window for Substrings without Repeating Characters, Frequency Arrays for ASCII Strings, and Prefix Sums
  - 13. Linked List Interview Questions: Iterative In-Place Reversal, Pointer Splicing, Floyd's Cycle Detection (Tortoise and Hare), Middle Node Finding, and Merging Sorted Lists
  - 14. Tree and Graph Interview Questions: Breadth-First Search (BFS) Level-Order Traversal with Queue, Depth-First Search (DFS) Tree Traversal, Graph Representation (Adjacency Lists), and Shortest Path in Unweighted Graphs
  - 15. Dynamic Programming Interview Questions: Identifying Overlapping Subproblems and Optimal Substructure, Memoization vs Tabulation, House Robber Optimization (O(1) Space Variables), Knapsack, and Subsequence Patterns
  - 16. Mock Technical Interviews: Simulating Live Technical Screenings, Time Management, Peer Rubrics, and Adapting to Unfamiliar Problem Statements
  - 17. Timed Coding Assessments: Online Assessment (OA) Tactics, 90-Minute 3-Problem Triage Strategy, Budgeting Time for Testing, and Handling Platform Edge Suites
  - 18. Competitive Programming Revision: Speed Patterns, Fast I/O, Binary Exponentiation, Bit Manipulation Tricks, and Modular Arithmetic
  - 19. Interview Mistake Analysis: Taxonomy of Technical and Behavioral Failures, Requirement Misunderstandings, Algorithm Mis-selection, Infinite Loops, and Maintaining an Interview Error Log
  - 20. Technical Interview Question Bank: High-Frequency Question Catalog Spanning Data Structures, Algorithms, Patterns, and System Foundations
  - 21. Practical Interview Preparation Strategy: 4-Phase Roadmap: Foundational Fluency, Pattern Drill, Timed Mock Assessments, and Company-Specific Calibration
  - 22. 35 Practice Problems Across 4 Levels: Core Fundamentals, Interview Patterns, Trees/Graphs/DP, and Mock Assessment Simulations
  - 23. 15 Comprehensive Assessment MCQs with Explanations and Instant Scorecards
  - 24. 8 Interactive Workbenches: 7-Step Coding Interview Workflow Simulator, Brute Force to Optimized Transformer, Systematic Dry-Run Simulator, Edge Case Stress Tester, Think-Explain-Implement Communication Trainer, Floyd's Cycle Detection Visualizer, Kadane's Subarray Max Step Visualizer, and Mock Interview Scoring & Mistake Diagnostic Matrix

### Module 24: Final Java & DSA Capstone Project
URL: https://prepspaces.com/learning/java/capstone-project
Topics Covered:
  - 1. Understanding the Three Capstone Projects: Comparative Evaluation of Project 1 (Interactive DSA Algorithm Visualizer), Project 2 (Java Coding Interview Platform), and Project 3 (Intelligent Data Structures Playground)

  - 3. Visualize Sorting Algorithms: Step-By-Step Mechanics for Bubble, Selection, Insertion, Merge, Quick, and Heap Sort with Operation Counters and Space/Time Asymptotics
  - 4. Visualize Searching Algorithms: Linear Search Traversal vs Binary Search Interval Halving, Pointer Tracking (Left, Mid, Right), and Sortedness Invariants
  - 5. Visualize Trees: Hierarchical Structures, Binary Search Tree (BST) Invariants, Insertion Animations, Searching Paths, In-Order Successor Deletion, and Traversals (Inorder, Preorder, Postorder, Level-Order)
  - 6. Visualize Graphs: Vertices, Edges, Weights, Breadth-First Search (BFS) Radial Exploration, Depth-First Search (DFS) Stack Backtracking, Dijkstra's Shortest Path with PriorityQueue Edge Relaxation, and Prim's Minimum Spanning Tree
  - 7. Dynamic Programming Visualization: Tabulation State Calculations, Overlapping Subproblems Highlighting, Fibonacci Table, Climbing Stairs, and 2D 0/1 Knapsack Decision Grids

  - 9. What is a Coding Interview Platform: Mini-LeetCode Architecture, Problem Management, Monaco Code Workspace, Judge Engine, Isolated Non-Root Docker Sandboxes, Resource Limits (CPU/Memory/Timeout), Verdict Evaluation (AC, WA, TLE, MLE, CE), Submission Histories, Leaderboards, and Relational Database Schemas

What is a Data Structures Playground: Implementing Collections from Scratch, Generic DynamicArray with 2x Geometric Doubling and System.arraycopy, Singly/Doubly LinkedLists, Separate Chaining HashMap with Bucket Resizing, AVL Self-Balancing Rotations (LL, RR, LR, RL), Logical Memory Reference Visualizations, and JMH Benchmarking

  - 15. Java Implementation Standards: Production OOP Standards, Encapsulation, Polymorphism, Interface Abstractions, Generic Collections, and Robust Defensive Exception Hierarchies
  - 16. Unit Testing: Automated Testing with JUnit 5, Unit vs Integration vs Regression Testing, and Test-Driven Development (TDD) Red-Green-Refactor Lifecycle
  - 17. What is Edge Case Testing: Defensive Input Validation Boundaries, Empty Collections, Single Elements, Duplicates, Negative Bounds, Integer Overflows, Disconnected Graphs, and Testing Matrices
  - 18. What is Performance Benchmarking: NanoTime Limitations, Java Microbenchmark Harness (JMH), JVM Warm-Up Cycles, Tiered Compilation Impact, and Big-O Scalability vs Physical Cache Hardware Latency
  - 19. Version Control: Git Repository Hygiene, Atomic Commits, Feature Branching Workflows, Conventional Commit Standards, .gitignore Configuration, and Public GitHub Deliverables
  - 20. Project Documentation: Professional README Authoring, System Architecture Diagrams, Installation Prerequisites, Complexity Matrices, and Empirical Testing Reports
  - 21. What is Deployment: Desktop Native Application Bundles with jpackage, Backend Docker Containerization, and Isolated Execution Worker Network Segmentation
  - 22. How to Present Your Project: Engineering Defense Structure, 11 Technical Talking Points, and 10-Slide Architecture Presentation Deck
  - 23. Implementation Phases: Controlled 10-Phase Roadmap: Requirements, Architecture, Data Structures, Algorithms, MVP Features, Testing, Optimization, Git/Docs, Deployment, and Defense
  - 24. How Should the Project Be Evaluated: 100% Weighted Assessment Rubric (OOP 15%, DSA 25%, Architecture 15%, Testing 15%, Performance 10%, Docs 10%, Deployment 10%) and 5 Competency Achievement Tiers
